correctness.rationale: With type frequencies 1/2, household fractions ((1-b)/2,b,(1-b)/2), and equal susceptibility weights, every contacted descendant household has the same pair-composition law as an ancestor. A type-i infective with partner j contributes Poisson mean beta_i or beta_i+beta_j according to Bernoulli p_ij local infection. This yields F_b=(1-b)F0+bF1 with F0=1/40u+19/40u^2+99/200u^5+1/200u^10 and F1=3/10u+99/200u^5+41/200u^6, u=e^(s-1). Means are 7/2 and 801/200, hence R*(b)=7/2+101b/200. On 0<=s<=1/5, u<=e^(-4/5)<1/2; rational upper bounds put F0,F1 below 1/5 at the endpoint, while F_b(0)>0, hence q_b is in (0,1/5). F1-F0=u(55-95u+41u^5-u^9)/200>0 throughout that strip (bracket >=3839/512), so the unique subunit fixed point q_b strictly increases with b and Pi=1-q_b strictly decreases. Strict compact uniform margins give perturbation stability for biological parameters. Independent rational coefficient/mean check and b=0,1/2,1 numerical roots confirmed without supplying an infinite proof.

value.rationale: An exact sign reversal along an entire natural fixed-composition household-matching continuum is a substantive and interpretable counterexample to using R* rankings for outbreak probability. The strict parameter robustness makes it more than an accidental numerical pair or arbitrary tiny finite improvement.
